notes: Path normalisation. The frontend axios client is created with baseURL '/api' (frontend/src/lib/http.ts, API_BASE_URL) and every service writes its path without that prefix, so `api.post('/clients')` is POST /api/clients at runtime. The backend declares the same prefix as API_PREFIX in backend/src/server.ts and mounts clientsRouter and settingsRouter at it, and invoicesRouter at `${API_PREFIX}/invoices`. The canonical path of an endpoint is the runtime path with the API base removed: mount point + registration path for the backend, and the written path for the frontend (already base-relative). Both sides therefore land on the same node, e.g. api:POST:/clients. Interpolated segments normalise to :param form named after the expression, so `/clients/${clientId}` and '/clients/:clientId' are one node. A backend path that is not under the API base is recorded verbatim (api:GET:/healthz) and can never join a frontend call. Confidence policy: 1.0 when source and target are in one module or one JSX expression; 0.95 when the hop crossed a module boundary and resolved to exactly one declaration; 0.9 when the edge needed several facts combined under a named rule. Tiers: 'core' edges must be found; 'stretch' edges are credit if found and no penalty if missed. `expectedRule` is null where no member of the current InferenceRule union covers the case; `ruleGap` then names the rule that would have to be added — those are findings, not fixture defects. Line numbers are asserted; this directory is prettier-ignored and eslint-ignored so they stay put. mustNotExist schema: every entry has `kind`. A node entry carries `idLike`, a canonical node id; `*` is legal only in the method position of an api: id and means "under any method". A relationship entry carries `type` and canonical `sourceLike`/`targetLike` ids. Optional `extra` narrows an assertion about an id the manifest also declares — 13 entries name a real node and forbid only a particular provenance or a second copy of it, so an id appearing here is never by itself a reason to drop the node.

exhaustiveness.element: complete, with one declared exception: element:client-detail.delete-dialog is in `ambiguous` because the literal id is forwarded on a prop, so an indexer that records it and one that does not are both within the manifest. Score element recall over the listed nodes; neither add nor subtract that id
exhaustiveness.api: complete for endpoints reachable from a *core* edge, with two declared exceptions. api:POST:/settings/api-key/rotate is reachable only through a stretch hop (the class service's injected client), so an indexer that skips that hop must not lose api recall for it; and api:GET:/healthz is in `ambiguous` because omitting an endpoint outside the API base is acceptable. Score api recall over the remaining nodes
exhaustiveness.service: complete for the declarations. The exported *instance* at services/settingsService.ts:53 is in `ambiguous`: recording it as a second service node is defensible and must not be scored as a false positive
exhaustiveness.hook: complete (project-declared hooks only; library hooks such as useState and useNavigate have no declaring file in the project and therefore no id under node-id.ts)
exhaustiveness.function: complete for named declarations, named function expressions, arrow functions bound to a name, object-literal methods and class methods — including the middleware returned by requirePermission/requireEveryPermission/validate/asyncHandler, the pool method in lib/db.ts, and `noop` in DashboardPage, all of which the previous revision claimed and omitted. Anonymous inline arrows are not function nodes. A component declaration wrapped in a call (forwardRef) is a component node and NOT also a function node — TextField is the one instance. Member naming for shorthand-aggregated services is in `ambiguous`: this manifest uses the member form (#invoiceService.list), and an indexer that uses the declaration form (#list) plus a mapping is differently addressed, not wrong, so those three ids must not be scored as misses
exhaustiveness.type: partial — only the aliases that exist to be mistaken for something else
exhaustiveness.relationships: complete for renders, contains, invokes, opens, submits_to, navigates_to, calls_api, requires_permission, validates_with, uses_hook and uses_service. `calls` is a SELECTION, not a set: it lists one representative edge per (calling module, callee) pair, chosen for the hardest hop, plus every service-member call. Of the cross-module calls to project-declared functions in this fixture it lists a minority on purpose — hasPermission has three call sites and db#query eleven, and repeating them proves nothing new. Recall must NOT be computed for `calls`: a number derived from this list measures how many representatives were picked, not how many calls were found
exhaustiveness.diagnostics: `expectedUnresolved` lists one representative site per *shape*, not every site. Emitting the same diagnostic at the other structurally identical sites is correct output and must not be scored as noise. For UNRESOLVED_DYNAMIC_CALL on a prop-bound handler those sites are ClientTable.tsx:60, ConfirmDeleteDialog.tsx:30, Dialog.tsx:26, Dialog.tsx:30 and ToolbarButton.tsx:22, in addition to the three listed. `expectedDiagnostics` is complete: it holds the cases that produce a node AND a diagnostic, which `expectedUnresolved` cannot express because that section means "must fail to resolve"

canonicalPathConvention: ADR 0006. An endpoint's identity is the fullest provable runtime path: the client baseURL or server mount prefix is applied, and path parameters are addressed positionally (:param) so a frontend ':id' and a backend ':clientId' cannot split one endpoint into two. The declared parameter name survives on the node's `path`. A router whose mount point is not provable is recorded with a '?' unknown-prefix marker and may never merge with a resolved endpoint.
